info.title: Device Uniqueness Backend
info.description:
**Prove the device and register the username on People Chain.**

### Validation flow

The iOS smoke drives this sequence end-to-end; each step gates the next:

1. `POST /api/v1/auth/challenges` — mint a single-use challenge
2. `POST /api/v1/auth/app-attest/attestations` — iOS App Attest (`202`, no-op in M0)
3. `POST /api/v1/auth/token` — sr25519 proof exchanged for a JWT
4. `POST /api/v1/usernames/available` — JWT-gated People Chain read
5. `POST /api/v1/usernames` — `202` outbox reservation

> **Attestation is disabled for M0.** Apple/Google verification is intentionally a no-op; the sr25519 account proof and People Chain reads still run end-to-end.

Errors come in two shapes. The auth handshake (`/api/v1/auth/*`) answers the `ErrorResponse` envelope — `{ error, message }`, where `error` is a stable machine code. Every other route answers `{ error }`, a human-readable summary, plus a `fields` array of `{ field, message }` when the failure is per-field validation.

get.summary: Publish the Ed25519 public key so siblings can verify tokens.
`GET /api/v1/attester` — the attester authority public key (`0x`+hex, public).

200.description: The on-chain attester account the backend writes as.

post.summary:
Register an App Attest key: verify the attestation object and persist the
credential key (no-op `202 {}` while `AUTH_ENABLED=false`).

202.description: Accepted. With attestation enabled, the key is verified against Apple and stored; while disabled, the payload is not verified.

401.description: Attestation rejected (hard mode), or the challenge was unknown, expired, or already used. Soft mode logs failed verdicts and returns 202.

201.description: A fresh single-use challenge. No body required.

post.summary: Verify challenge + client proof and issue an access + refresh token pair.

parameters.name: Auth-ClientId
parameters.description: Base64 of the 32-byte sr25519 public key.

parameters.name: Auth-ClientProof
parameters.description: Base64 of the 64-byte sr25519 signature over the raw body.

parameters.name: Auth-iOS-Package
parameters.description: iOS bundle id, e.g. io.pcf.polkadotapp. Selects the App Attest verification path.

parameters.name: Auth-Payload
parameters.description: Base64 App Attest assertion (iOS) or the raw classic Play Integrity token (Android play-integrity), verified when attestation is enabled.

parameters.name: Auth-iOS-KeyId
parameters.description: Base64 App Attest key id registered via /auth/app-attest/attestations.

parameters.name: Auth-Android-Package
parameters.description: Android package name; required for play-integrity and sets the JWT platform claim for Android clients.

parameters.name: Auth-Attestation-Type
parameters.description: Android attestation dispatch: `key-attestation` verifies the `attestationChain` field in the JSON body (base64 DER, leaf first), and also sets the Android platform claim when Auth-Android-Package is absent; `play-integrity` verifies the token in Auth-Payload with self-managed response keys.

requestBody.description: Raw body covered by the proof; may be empty {}. Android key-attestation requests carry the certificate chain here as `attestationChain` (2-10 base64 DER entries, leaf first).

200.description: Verified. Access JWT + opaque refresh token.

401.description: Bad or spent challenge, or invalid client proof.

503.description: Android attestation revocation list unavailable; retry with a fresh challenge (hard enforcement).

post.summary: Rotate a refresh token, returning a fresh access + refresh pair.

200.description: Rotated. New access JWT + new opaque refresh token.

401.description: Unknown, expired, or already-spent refresh token.

get.summary: Registration-queue standing for the authenticated account.
get.description: Queue standing for the caller's pending username claim. This route exists only on deployments with the registration queue enabled (`QUEUE_ENABLED`); with the queue disabled the path serves the standard plain-text 404. Clients should treat ANY 404 here as "not (or no longer) queued" and assume the registration is proceeding — queued claims keep draining even if the queue is later disabled. When an account has several queued claims, the response reports the earliest-enqueued one until it drains.

200.description: The caller's queued claim: position, priority group, and the estimated advancer iterations until it is promoted for on-chain registration.

404.description: The account has no queued registration (JSON body), or the deployment runs queue-disabled (plain-text body). Either way: stop polling, the claim is proceeding without the queue.

post.summary: Reserve a lite username and enqueue it for on-chain registration.

200.description: The device is not eligible for a free registration: hard-mode DeviceCheck found its free slot already used, enforced Widevine dedup found the device already recorded or the Android claim carried no evidence, or a concurrent claim won the device's slot. Not an error — a 200 outcome, and a terminal one: no claim is stored and there is no paid alternative. The value `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` is historical (the retired paid lane) and kept for client compatibility.

202.description: Reservation accepted into the outbox for on-chain registration. With the registration queue enabled (`QUEUE_ENABLED`) and the queue service live, the claim waits in the balance-priority queue and the body additionally carries `registrationOutcome: "QUEUED"` plus the claim's queue standing (poll `GET /api/v1/registration/queue` for updates). A down queue service falls back to the direct registration path (no queue fields). With `REGISTRATION_VOUCHERS_ENABLED`, a valid `lifetimePoUDVoucher` bypasses the device gate and the queue: the reservation goes straight to the writer and the body carries `registrationOutcome: "INSTANT"`.

400.description: Validation failed (with per-field `fields`), malformed JSON, a `lifetimePoUDVoucher` that is unknown, already used, or expired (`{"error": "Voucher already used"}` — a voucher failure rejects the claim outright), or — with `WIDEVINE_DEDUP_ENFORCE` — structurally malformed device evidence (`{"error": "DEVICE_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED"}`: partial fields, bad base64, or wrong field sizes — the specific reason is logged server-side, never returned).

example.error: The request body contains invalid values.

401.description: Missing or invalid bearer token, or hard-mode DeviceCheck required a usable Device-Token-iOS and none was present.

403.description: Device evidence failed verification under `WIDEVINE_DEDUP_ENFORCE`: chain policy, the cert-bound evidence hash (challenge / account / deviceId), or a spent challenge. The specific reason is logged server-side, never returned. Retryable once with a fresh challenge; a claim retried without evidence gets the 200 ineligible outcome.

409.description: Preferred digits taken, no digits available, username taken, or the claim carries `dotns.reservedUsername` for a personhood name that is already owned or whose reservation queue is full — checked against the reserved name itself, which `attest` takes as its own argument and which need not be `username`. The runtime checks that leg *before* it writes the lite username, and the consumer signature covers it, so submitting would cost the whole registration and no server-side retry could rescue it. Re-sign for another `dotns.reservedUsername`.

example.error: Preferred digits 07 already taken for username tallesx

502.description: Hard-mode DeviceCheck could not reach Apple to resolve the device.

503.description: The DeviceCheck free slot could not be marked used at Apple after a successful gate (upstream write failure; retryable), or the enforced Widevine dedup gate could not fetch the attestation revocation list (`DEVICE_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE`; retryable).

example.error: Failed to mark iOS device as registered with Apple DeviceCheck

200.description: Per-base availability read from People Chain UsernameOwnerOf plus pending outbox reservations, tagged `{_tag: "v1", value}` with availableDigits. `EXHAUSTED` means nothing claimable under this base: no free discriminator, or the bare personhood name is owned or its reservation queue is full — the last two would make a claim carrying `dotns.reservedUsername` fail on chain and take the lite username with it.

example.error: The request body contains invalid values.

500.description: People Chain failure or reservation-outbox failure.

example.error: Internal server error. Please try again.

get.summary: Process health probe. No dependencies checked.

200.description: Process is up. No dependencies checked.

get.summary: Kubernetes liveness probe — "should this pod be restarted".
Kubernetes readiness probe — checks `db` and `chain` subsystems.

200.description: Instance can take traffic; db and chain reachable.

post.summary: Issue a proof-of-compute puzzle for an unauthenticated caller.

201.description: A fresh puzzle to solve. Mine a `counter` whose `sha256(sessionId || timestamp || counter)` has at least `difficulty` leading zero bits, then send `Proof-Of-Compute: base64(sessionId:timestamp:difficulty:counter:checksum)` on the search request. Callers holding an device-attestation JWT do not need a puzzle.

404.description: Proof of compute is disabled on this deployment (`POC_ENABLED=false`): the route is not mounted and the service-wide 404 answers instead.

get.summary: Public prefix search over the finalized username projection.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Prefix of letters/digits, optionally followed by a dot and digits.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Requested page size, defaulting to 100 and clamped to 1,000.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation cursor from an earlier response.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Optional `Bearer <JWT>` from device-attestation. When proof of compute is enabled, a valid token satisfies this route and no puzzle is needed. An unverifiable token is treated as anonymous — this route never answers 401.

parameters.name: Proof-Of-Compute
parameters.description: Solved puzzle, required only when proof of compute is enabled and no valid bearer token is presented: `base64(sessionId:timestamp:difficulty:counter:checksum)` for a puzzle from `POST /api/v1/poc/issue`. Single-use.

200.description: Matching assigned usernames in continuation order. Registrations whose on-chain identifier key predates chat-spec RFC-0004 (pre-X25519) are omitted — the app cannot message them.

400.description: Invalid query parameter (with per-field `fields`), invalid cursor (`{"error":"Invalid cursor"}`), or a malformed `Proof-Of-Compute` header.

example.error: The request query contains invalid values.

402.description: Proof of compute is enabled and the caller presented neither a valid bearer token nor an acceptable puzzle. The `error` names the reason: missing proof, checksum mismatch, expired puzzle, already-used puzzle, or insufficient difficulty.

example.error: Proof of compute required. Request a puzzle from POST /api/v1/poc/issue and present the solved proof in the Proof-Of-Compute header.
Rate limit exceeded. Please retry after 60 seconds.

post.summary: Claim an invitation ticket for a DIM, returning a signature (JWT-gated).

200.description: Ticket claimed: the oldest `available` ticket of the `(dim, network)` pool, atomically flipped to `claimed`, with an sr25519 signature by the ticket key over the claimant's decoded 32-byte account id.

400.description: Body validation failed (with per-field `fields`), or `Malformed JSON in request body` when the body is not JSON.

401.description: Missing/malformed `Authorization` header or failed token verification.

409.description: Ticket race lost — a concurrent request claimed the contended ticket.

422.description: Pool exhausted — no `available` ticket in the `(dim, network)` pool.

post.summary: Issue short-lived TURN credentials for WebRTC ICE negotiation (JWT-gated).

201.description: Credentials issued: `username` and `password` are an opaque pair from the deployment's configured `TURN_PROVIDER` — do not parse either — `servers` is the ICE server list to use them against, and `ttl` is the seconds of life remaining on the credential.

400.description: Body validation failed (with per-field `fields`), or `Malformed JSON in request body` when a body is present but not JSON. An empty body is accepted — every field is optional.

401.description: Missing/malformed `Authorization` header or failed token verification.

503.description: The credential provider could not issue and no cached credential was usable (with `Retry-After`). Only reachable on the Cloudflare provider, which depends on an upstream call; a coturn deployment computes credentials locally and never returns this.

post.summary: Redeem a personhood proof for the same credentials as `/turn/issue`.

201.description: Proof accepted; returns the servers and an opaque username/password pair from the configured `TURN_PROVIDER`, and `ttl`, the seconds of life remaining on them. No alias appears in the response, and nothing recoverable from the proof is derivable from the credential.

400.description: Unparseable body, invalid hex, a collection outside the canonical People Lite/People allowlist, a proof that is not a single-context ring-VRF signature, a product this deployment does not accept, or a timestamp outside the accepted skew.

403.description: The proof did not verify against the named ring root under that product's context — including when `(ringIndex, ringRevision)` is outside the roots this deployment still holds (deliberately unspecific).

429.description: This person's redemption limit was exceeded (with `Retry-After`).

503.description: Verification unavailable: no ring-root snapshot yet (chain unreachable since boot), the bounded waiter queue is full, or all verification slots remained busy for the bounded wait. Also returned when the proof verified but the credential provider could not issue and no cached credential was usable, which only the Cloudflare provider can do. Saturation and provider responses include `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Order mirrors the sibling services: verified JWT (`401` problem details) →
body parse (`400` plain text on malformed JSON) → body validation (`400`
problem details with per-field `errors`) → per-subject rate limit (`429`
with `Retry-After`). Beyond that the relay always answers `200`: on provider
failure it preserves the legacy `success: false` body instead of an error
status.

200.description: Relay accepted the request. The push result is echoed verbatim from the provider — including the legacy behavior of returning `200` with `success: false` on provider failure, so a non-200 status never signals a delivery failure.

400.description: Body validation failed (RFC 9457 problem details with per-field `errors`); or plain-text `Malformed JSON in request body` when the body is not JSON.

401.description: Missing/malformed `Authorization` header or failed token verification (RFC 9457 problem details).

429.description: Per-subject rate limit exceeded (RFC 9457 problem details, with `Retry-After`).

AppAttestRequest.description: iOS Apple App Attest key-registration payload.

keyId.description: Base64 key identifier (SHA-256 of the credential public key).

attestation.description: Base64 CBOR attestation object from the platform.

AttesterResponse.description: `{ attester }` — the on-chain attester authority public key.

attester.description: `0x`-hex sr25519 public key the backend writes registrations as.

AvailableRequest.description:
`{ usernames: [base, ...] }` — bases to validate and check on chain
(documentation mirror; the handler validates raw JSON).

usernames.description: Candidate base usernames to validate and check (max 100).

value.description: Per-base availability, keyed by the requested base username.

ChallengeResponse.description: `201` body: a fresh single-use challenge for the sr25519 proof flow.

challenge.description: Opaque base64 32-byte challenge; echoed back in the `Auth-Challenge` header.

Dotns.description: Optional DotNS reservation, parking a base label for later personhood use.

signedAt.description: Unix timestamp the reservation was signed at.

reservedUsername.description:
The bare personhood name to reserve. Its own name on chain — it need
not be `username`, and availability is checked against *this* name, not
against the base of the lite username in the same claim.

ErrorResponse.description:
The shared error envelope returned by every non-2xx response.

`error` is a stable machine code (see [`AppError`]); `message` is a
human-readable detail that may change. This type exists so the OpenAPI
document can reference a single error schema across all endpoints.

message.description: Human-readable detail; safe to log, not intended for programmatic use.

NameAvailability.description: Availability of a single base username.

status.description: `AVAILABLE`, `EXHAUSTED` (nothing claimable under this base), or `INVALID` (fails base rules).

QueueStatusResponse.description:
Queue standing for one claim, as served by `GET /api/v1/registration/queue`
and embedded in the claim response's `queue` field.

queuePosition.description: 1-based position in the drain order of the current queue snapshot.

group.description: Priority group `1..=4` (4 = highest; raised by topping up the account).

estimatedIterationsRemaining.description: Advancer iterations until promotion, per the snapshot simulation.

RefreshRequest.description: `{ refreshToken }` — present a prior opaque refresh token to rotate it.

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token issued by `/auth/token` or a prior refresh.

RegisterRequest.description:
The flat registration request (documentation mirror — the handler
validates raw JSON so it can report every failing field).

candidateAccountId.description: SS58 beneficiary account that will own the username.

preferredDigits.description: Optional two-digit suffix, e.g. `"07"`; random-free if omitted.

candidateSignature.description: `0x`-hex 64-byte sr25519 signature proving control of the candidate.

lifetimePoUDVoucher.description:
Optional single-use registration voucher (the INSTANT lane): bypasses
the PoUD gate and the registration queue. Ignored unless
`REGISTRATION_VOUCHERS_ENABLED`.

attestationChain.description:
Optional Android device-uniqueness evidence (Widevine PoUD): leaf-first
base64 DER attestation chain, 2-10 entries, whose leaf key was created
with `attestationChallenge = SHA-256(domain ‖ deviceChallenge ‖
accountKey ‖ deviceId)`. All three evidence fields are present
together or not at all; ignored unless `WIDEVINE_DEDUP_ENABLED`.
Sent only when the app measured Widevine L1.

deviceChallenge.description:
Base64 32-byte single-use challenge from `/auth/challenges`, bound
into the leaf key's attestation challenge.

deviceId.description:
Base64 32-byte device pseudonym:
`SHA-256("dub/poud/widevine-id/v1" ‖ rawWidevineId)`, computed on the
device — the raw id never leaves it.

RegisterResponse.description: `202` body: the reserved full username and its parts.

device_check_available.description:
Present only when the DeviceCheck free-slot gate ran and produced an
advisory availability (`Register`/`Proceed`); omitted when DeviceCheck
is disabled or the outcome short-circuited (ineligible/token/unavailable).

registrationOutcome.description:
`"QUEUED"` when the registration queue is enabled and the claim is
waiting in it; `"INSTANT"` when a voucher bypassed the gate and the
queue; absent on the plain direct-to-writer path. (The
`PAYMENT_REQUIRED` outcome is a separate `200` body, not this 202
shape — see the route's 200 response.)

oneOf.description:
Queue standing at claim time (present only with
`registrationOutcome: "QUEUED"`).

Status.description: A liveness/health status body: `{ status, service }`.

TokenResponse.description: `{ token, refreshToken }` — the shape both auth token routes return.

Puzzle.description: A freshly issued puzzle, serialized as the frozen `201` body.

sessionId.description: Opaque puzzle identifier (UUID); the replay-protection key.

timestamp.description: Issue time in unix milliseconds; bounds the puzzle's validity.

difficulty.description: Required number of leading zero bits in the work digest.

checksum.description:
Lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256 over the puzzle fields; proves this server
issued the puzzle, so nothing is stored at issue time.

usernames.description: Assigned usernames in deterministic continuation order.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when exhausted.

SearchUsername.description: One assigned username in the shipping mobile response shape.

accountId.description: People Chain account encoded as SS58.

username.description:
The username exactly as the chain holds it: the full username when
present, otherwise the lite username with its suffix unchanged
(`alice.06`, never `alice.6` — the padded form is the only one
`UsernameOwnerOf` answers to).

status.description: Assignment state, always `ASSIGNED` for this projection.

createdAt.description: Time the projection first observed the account.

updatedAt.description: Time the projection last refreshed the account.

who.description: SS58 address to claim a ticket for (any valid SS58 prefix).

dim.description: DIM to claim a ticket for: `Game` or `ProofOfInk`.

ClaimResponse.description:
The 200 claim body: the ticket keypair's public half plus the
sr25519 signature over the claimant's decoded account id.

publicKey.description: `0x`-hex 32-byte sr25519 public key of the claimed ticket.

inviter.description: SS58 address of the inviter that registered the ticket on-chain.

network.description: Network the ticket is registered on: `westend2`, `paseo`, or `polkadot`.

claimedBy.description: SS58 address the ticket was claimed for (echoes `who`).

createdAt.description: Ticket generation time (JS-style ISO, millisecond precision).

signature.description:
`0x`-hex 64-byte sr25519 signature by the ticket key over the raw
32-byte account id decoded from `who`.

remaining.description: Tickets still `available` in this `(dim, network)` pool after the claim.

IssueRequest.description: `{ regionHint? }` — the issue command (the hint is reserved and ignored).

regionHint.description: Optional region hint (reserved for future use; accepted and ignored).

IssueResponse.description:
The 201 body: an ephemeral TURN credential and the ICE servers to use it
against.

Both fields' provenance depends on the deployment's `TURN_PROVIDER`, and the
shape of `username`/`password` differs between them — treat both as opaque
strings to stay portable across providers.

servers.description:
The ICE server URLs (`stun:` / `turn:` / `turns:` forms) to negotiate
against. On the Cloudflare provider these are what Cloudflare returned
with the credential, flattened into one list in response order; on the
coturn provider they are the operator's configured `ICE_SERVERS`.

username.description:
The credential's username. **Opaque — do not parse.** Cloudflare mints
an unstructured value per request; a coturn deployment uses that relay's
REST-API form, `{unixExpiry}:{hexId}`. Neither carries anything
recoverable about the caller.

password.description:
The matching password. **Opaque — do not parse.** Minted by Cloudflare,
or on the coturn provider the base64 HMAC over `username` under the
relay-shared secret.

ttl.description:
Seconds of life remaining on this credential. On the coturn provider
always the configured `TURN_TTL_SECS`, since the credential is minted to
order. On the Cloudflare provider the TTL Cloudflare granted, or less if
a cached credential was served because Cloudflare was briefly
unreachable.

productId.description:
The product the proof was made for. Its context is the one the proof
is verified under, so a product proves under its own identifier. Must
be one this deployment accepts.

collection.description:
Hex-encoded 32-byte collection id from the proof's TrUAPI
`ringLocation`. Only the canonical People Lite and People collections
are accepted.

proof.description:
Ring-VRF proof over the derived message (hex), exactly as the host
returns it — raw signature bytes, with no SCALE length prefix.

ringIndex.description: Ring containing the proving member, used to locate the root.

ringRevision.description:
Revision of that ring the proof was made against, as the host reports
it. Only that revision's root is tried, so a revision this deployment
no longer holds is refused without verifying anything.

timestamp.description:
Client Unix seconds, bound into the proved message. Must be within the
server's accepted skew.

NotifyErrorDoc.description: One per-device push error inside the `200` response.

device.description: Device token the error is about.

environment.description: APNs environment, when the provider distinguishes dev/prod.

status.description: Provider status (string or number), when present.

deviceToken.description: Recipient device token (APNs hex or FCM token); platform is auto-detected.

pushId.description: Opaque push id echoed to the client app (32 or 64 hex chars).

platform.description: Explicit platform override; auto-detected from the token when omitted.

bundlerId.description: APNs topic override (the app bundle id); VoIP derives `<topic>.voip`.

voip.description: Enable the iOS VoIP push type for a call.

NotifyResponseDoc.description: The frozen `200` push-result body (echoed from the provider).

success.description: Whether the provider accepted the push.

platform.description: Platform the notification was routed to.

sent.description: Number of notifications sent, when the provider reports it (APNs/FCM).

failed.description: Number of failed notifications, when the provider reports it (APNs).

errors.description: Per-device errors, on partial or full provider failure.

tags.name: Usernames
tags.description: Public username search over the finalized chain projection. Served to callers with an device-attestation JWT or, when proof of compute is enabled, a solved puzzle; rate-limited per subject or client IP.

tags.name: Proof of compute
tags.description: Puzzle issuance for callers that hold no bearer token. Mounted only when `POC_ENABLED=true`.

tags.name: Invitation Tickets
tags.description: Synchronous invitation-credential claims from a pre-staged, on-chain-registered sr25519 keypair pool. The route the shipping iOS/Android apps call for Game / ProofOfInk credentials.

tags.name: TURN
tags.description: Short-lived TURN credentials for WebRTC ICE negotiation. The credential source is the deployment's `TURN_PROVIDER`: **Cloudflare Realtime TURN** (the default), which mints each credential itself — one per request, so callers are mutually unlinkable, with the last response cached and served if Cloudflare is briefly unreachable — or a self-hosted **coturn** relay, where this service computes the credential from a secret shared with the relay and callers are kept unlinkable by an opaque keyed id instead. Either way nothing is persisted. Issuance is authorized either by an access JWT (`/issue`) or, when enabled, by a personhood ring-VRF proof over a client-timestamped message (`/issue-with-proof`).

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: Send a push notification to an iOS (APNs) or Android (FCM) device. Stateless verify-only relay: it authenticates the JWT and forwards the frozen mobile payload, returning the provider's result — including the legacy `200 success:false` on provider failure.
